A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M3DLayout and retain matching dataset construction and benchmark material. Text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion-model experiments and source ablations in Table 3, generated layouts, and a 42-participant perceptual study in Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds autoregressive-model results, source ablations, and generation-time measurements in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: v2 adds an autoregressive Transformer encoder alongside the diffusion generator. It predicts objects sequentially from text and preceding objects, uses start/end tokens, and minimizes object-parameter negative log-likelihood (Sections 4.3 and 8.2). This is a distinct generation procedure.

E1.justification: The three data sources, 26 scene categories, and bedroom/dining-room/living-room evaluation coverage remain unchanged. Although v2 enlarges Inf3DLayout, Section 8.1 explicitly retains the original 15,080-scene experimental subset. No new task, domain, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds AR-M3DLayout to the comparison alongside the retained diffusion model, DiffuScene, and InstructScene. The external comparator set, including its participation in the qualitative comparison and user study, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported diffusion optimizer changes from AdamW in v1 Appendix A.1 to Adam in v2 Section 8.3; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun. v2 also introduces autoregressive training settings and timing metrics. Existing splits, 1,500 test prompts, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends supplementary analysis with source-specific autoregressive ablations (Table 5), computational-efficiency comparisons (Table 4), and five additional prompt-adherence examples (Figure 11). The earlier diffusion ablations are retained in Table 5, not removed.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the same user-study means and error bars, without newly explaining their statistical meaning. Model results remain point estimates; neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported dataset totals increase from 15,080 layouts and 258,413 objects to 21,367 and 433,842, with revised distribution statistics. New results include AR-M3DLayout's Inf3DLayout FID of 57.90 and CLIP-Score of 0.2026, three autoregressive ablation rows, and timing measurements. Existing diffusion, external-baseline, and user-study results are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds the autoregressive conditional-likelihood factorization and its negative-log-likelihood training formulation. The diffusion reverse distribution and noise-prediction objective are retained. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a multi-source dataset with structured descriptions. v2 increases the claimed resource size and broadens the benchmark contribution to diffusion and autoregression. It also replaces v1's introduction claim of consistent improvements from progressively adding sources with a narrower statement about supporting diversity and detail.

C2.justification: Section 10 extends the single-source overfitting and multi-source generalization interpretation to autoregressive models. The introduction adds an argument connecting part-level object generation and scene generation through enriched bounding boxes. Existing explanations of diffusion results and the limitation concerning language-model annotation noise remain.

D1.justification: Sections 8.2–8.3 substantially expand implementation disclosure, specifying 120-object padding, coordinate ordering, orientation encoding, BERT conditioning, attribute embeddings, diffusion learning-rate decay, and autoregressive training details. These disclosures do not establish changes to the existing diffusion procedure. The abstract also newly promises dataset and code release upon acceptance, without establishing actual availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds AutoPartGen, OmniPart, X-Part, and CoPart, with an introduction paragraph positioning layouts as a bridge between part-level object generation and scene generation. The existing indoor-dataset and scene-synthesis related-work discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: The unified Benchmark section becomes separate Indoor Scene Generation and Experiments sections. Appendix A is reorganized into a supplement with an overview and dedicated implementation, visualization, ablation, and retrieval sections; references move behind supplementary text. Motivation and model explanations are also expanded.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout, substantially resizing figures and tables. The original Table 3 is split between benchmark and supplementary ablation tables. v2 adds a timing table and autoregressive/prompt-adherence figures, while retaining and relocating earlier visual material.

improvement.justification: The autoregressive benchmark and source ablations broaden evidence for the dataset's utility, while Section 8 substantially improves implementation disclosure. These gains support a limited net improvement: the enlarged corpus is not experimentally evaluated, timing results lack hardware and measurement controls, and the optimizer revision is not reconciled with unchanged diffusion scores.
